page: Amazon Web Services r5n.4xlarge is a memory-optimized, network-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 16 vCPUs, corresponding to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading, running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached EBS storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance, including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, falls into the lower 25% tier. However, multi-core execution and memory bandwidth tests, such as large-block uncached memory reads at 87.18 GB/sec and writes at 48.4 GB/sec, consistently achieve average tier results. The instance also demonstrates average performance in database operations, Redis SET operations at 13.18 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 11.9 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5n.4xlarge offers a high-density memory configuration suitable for memory-bound applications without the overhead of premium compute-heavy processors. The primary tradeoff is the weaker single-threaded performance, making it less suitable for single-core intensive tasks. It is highly optimized for workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, mid-sized database management systems, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines that benefit from its 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.
